intro: Khao Lak is a stretch of the Phang Nga coast that's several notches quieter than Phuket or Krabi. Most people who come here are after the sound of the waves and a real rest, not nightlife · X10 Khaolak Resort is a 4-star beachfront resort in the Khuk Khak (Bang La On) area, sitting between Nang Thong and Bang Niang beaches · what people talk about most is that it has 5 pools, one of which is reserved for adults only, so families with young kids and couples wanting some quiet can both stay in the same place without getting in each other's way · it's split into 2 wings — Family Wing and Beach Wing — with a Kids Suite that has bunk beds just for the children · from about THB 2,800/night · scored 9.0 from 323 Booking reviews and 4.7 on TripAdvisor (ranked #3 of 14 hotels in Khuk Khak)

body.html: Who X10 Khaolak suits — in the shortest possible summary, X10 Khaolak Resort is a resort designed so that "families and couples can stay together without fighting over space" · it isn't a tiny boutique resort selling maximum privacy, and it isn't a downtown hotel where you step out into shops and restaurants right away · it's a large beachfront resort of around 284 rooms with a clearly split structure of 2 wings: Family Wing for families travelling with kids, and Beach Wing which sits closer to the sand · what people remember it for is that it has 5 pools, and the one closest to the beach is set aside as an adults-only pool (under-16s not allowed) — a detail you don't often find in a family resort at this price · real reviews line up on the same point: the people who fit here are families with kids from toddlers to teens, couples who want a beachfront resort without paying five-star prices, and anyone who wants an easy Khao Lak stay with plenty of in-resort activities · if you're after a small, very quiet resort focused on privacy, or want a room with bold design, this may not be your first answer, because its character is a family resort that gets lively around the pools during the day

Location and getting there — X10 Khaolak Resort sits in the Khuk Khak area, the side many people call the Bang La On zone, set between Nang Thong and Bang Niang — two of Khao Lak's most popular beaches · the strength of the location is that it's truly beachfront, you can walk straight down to the sea from the resort, and it's still a short drive or ride from the restaurant strips and markets · Bang Niang Market, a popular tourist night market, is about 2–3 km away, while Nang Thong Beach and Pakarang Beach are around a 10 min drive · for getting in from further afield, the resort is about 60–75 min by car from Phuket Airport (HKT) depending on traffic — most people have the resort or a transfer company arrange a pickup in advance, since taxis in Khao Lak are harder to find than in a big city · one note that comes up in reviews is that some people say the resort is "a little out of town and away from the shops," so if you want to walk out for every meal you may need a car or a rental motorbike, but if you're mainly here to relax the location is just right — you get both a quiet beach and convenience within easy reach

"We came as three families. The kids spent all day on the slide pool and at the kids club, while the parents slipped off to the adults-only pool on the quiet beach side for a drink — the most well-balanced place we've ever stayed with young kids."

Room types and decor — X10 Khaolak splits its rooms clearly by wing · on the Family Wing side there's Deluxe (sleeps 2 adults + 1 child), Deluxe Triple which adds a sofa bed for 3, Deluxe Pool View overlooking the pool, and the Kids Suite, the highlight of this side — a room with a separate kids' room with bunk beds and two bathrooms, great for families who want the children to have their own space · on the Beach Wing side, closer to the sea, there's Deluxe, Deluxe Pool View, Deluxe Pool Access on the ground floor where you can step straight down to the pool from your balcony, and a smaller Kids Suite that's closer to the beach · there are also suite-class rooms like the Couple Suite and Two Bedroom Suite for couples or larger families, and some suite-class rooms have a small kitchenette and a coffee machine · the decor is contemporary in a bright, clean tone, leaning toward easy use rather than flashy design · many reviews agree the rooms are very clean, modern, and well-equipped with a flat-screen TV, tea/coffee maker, safe, and a private balcony · one note that crops up in reviews is that some rooms use a glass door to separate the bathroom, so privacy may not be 100% for some people, and the extra bed is sometimes not as comfortable as the main bed — details worth considering if several of you are sharing one room

Facilities, pools, and spa — the heart of X10 Khaolak is its 5 pools spread across both wings · the pools are designed with shallow areas that slope in gradually and curved edges, suiting kids of all ages · there are 2 kids' pools with slides and a splash zone for little ones, the main reason families choose this place · at the same time, the pool closest to the beach is set aside as an adults-only pool (under-16s not allowed), so couples or adults who want some quiet still get their own corner within the same resort · there's a swim-up pool bar where you can swim over and order drinks, and a beach bar for watching the sunset · the pools are open roughly 8:00 AM–8:00 PM · besides the pools there's The Sun Spa offering Thai massage, body scrubs, facials, and nails, a fitness room with an aerobics room, a kids club open around 9:00 AM–5:00 PM, pool and ping-pong tables, non-motorized water activities, and a mini-shop with an ATM in the resort · to be honest, the pools here aren't long lap pools for serious swimming workouts, but they're recreational pools that do a good job on fun and on splitting the zones up for each group

Food and bars — the main restaurant at X10 Khaolak is Seaside Seafood Kitchen, an open terrace set between the pool and the beach, serving a la carte seafood and Thai food · several reviews praise the Thai food here as tasty and made with care, especially the seafood dishes with that seaside dining setting · breakfast is a varied buffet with both Asian and Western options, often praised for its variety and frequently fresh produce · there's a beach bar for evening cocktails and a swim-up pool bar for light snacks while you're in the water · to put it plainly, some voices in reviews say the in-resort dinner is a buffet at certain times, and the options may feel repetitive for guests staying several nights, and a few people have mentioned birds coming around the buffet at the main restaurant · because the location is a little out from the restaurant strips, many families eat mainly in the resort and head out to try places around Bang Niang or Nang Thong now and then — if you plan to eat out often, it's worth lining up a car or a rental motorbike

Service — staff is the point X10 Khaolak gets praised for most consistently in real reviews · on Booking the staff category scores as high as around 9.4, reflecting a team that's friendly, helpful, and attentive to detail · many reviews mention a warm welcome and help with kids' activities, arranging tours, and calling cars · the kids club staff and the poolside team often get a positive mention for looking after the children · but to be fair, some voices say the housekeeping details are sometimes inconsistent — for example, clearing things away too quickly or not refilling the water glasses, and sometimes the room you actually get doesn't exactly match the type you booked · overall, service is still a strength that brings people back for repeat stays and earns recommendations

What real reviews say (the good and the critical) — pulling from Booking.com, TripAdvisor, and Trip.com, the picture is fairly consistent · On the praise side: lots of pools that are fun for kids, the separate adults-only pool that gives couples a quiet space, clean and modern rooms, a varied breakfast, tasty Thai food, friendly and attentive staff, and a beachfront location that's great for taking kids down for a swim · On the critical side: what gets mentioned is that the location is a little away from the shops and town, so you need a car to eat out often, the buffet dinner options can feel repetitive on a long stay, the bathroom glass door in some rooms where privacy isn't 100%, the extra bed that isn't as comfortable as the main one, and sometimes the room you get not matching the type booked · there are also reviews noting that pool access for wheelchair users isn't very convenient, a point worth asking about in advance if someone in your group needs special facilities · most of these gripes can be managed by choosing the right room and setting expectations correctly, rather than being a major problem

"The room was very clean, the staff were lovely and helpful with everything, and breakfast had loads of choices · the only catch is that if you want to eat at a place outside the resort you have to take a car out — next time we'll just rent one."

Price and value comparison — the starting price for a Deluxe room is about THB 2,800/night in normal periods, climbing to around THB 4,500–6,500+ in high season or on long weekends · the Pool Access, Kids Suite, and Suite rooms sit from around THB 4,500 up into the low five figures depending on size and timing · compared with family beachfront resorts of the same class in Khao Lak, X10 feels very good value among family-focused 4-star resorts, especially counting that it has 5 pools, a separate adults-only pool, a kids club, and a Kids Suite designed specifically for children · compared with luxury resorts like The Sarojin or Casa de la Flora, which cost more and lean toward adult privacy, X10 suits families who want plenty of water play and space for the kids on a more attainable budget · for those planning to stay several nights with swimming as the main activity for the kids, the money spent comes back in full

Good to know before booking — there are several things that help the stay go smoothly · one, pick the wing that matches your style — if you're with young kids and want to be near the kids club and slide pool, choose Family Wing; if you'd rather be near the beach and the adults-only pool, choose Beach Wing · two, if you're travelling as a group or with several kids, the Kids Suite with bunk beds and two bathrooms is better value and more convenient than adding an extra bed · three, if bathroom privacy matters to you, ask about the glass door at the time of booking · four, plan your Phuket Airport transfer in advance, since it's about 60–75 min away and taxis are hard to find in Khao Lak · five, in Khao Lak's high season (November–April) rooms fill up fast and prices rise, so book ahead and compare prices across several platforms, and pick a free cancellation option first if your plans aren't firm yet

Summary — from all the real reviews, X10 Khaolak Resort is the best fit for families travelling with kids and couples who want a Khao Lak beachfront resort on an attainable budget, with pools and activities all sorted · having 5 pools, a separate adults-only pool, slides, a kids club, and a bunk-bed Kids Suite makes it suit families so well that it's hard to find a rival at the same price that splits the space up for each group this neatly · if you're after a small, very quiet resort focused on maximum privacy, a room with bold design, or want to walk straight out to restaurants, this may not be your first answer, and you should look at The Sarojin, Casa de la Flora, or a small boutique resort in this set instead · but for a family trip where you want the kids swimming all day, the adults to have their own corner to relax, and to fall asleep to the waves on Khao Lak beach at a reasonable price — X10 Khaolak gets just about everything right, which is why it keeps holding a high score and a top ranking in the area

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — X10 Khaolak Resort, Khao Lak Phang Nga

faq.q: Where is X10 Khaolak Resort and how do you get there?
faq.a: X10 Khaolak Resort sits on Phetkasem Road, Khuk Khak, Takua Pa district, Phang Nga province, on Khao Lak beach in the Khuk Khak (Bang La On) area between Nang Thong and Bang Niang beaches · it's about 2–3 km from Bang Niang Market and about 60–75 min by car from Phuket Airport (HKT) · taxis in Khao Lak are hard to find, so it's best to have the resort or a transfer company arrange a pickup in advance

faq.q: What's the starting price at X10 Khaolak Resort and what rooms are there?
faq.a: Prices start at about THB 2,800/night for a Deluxe room in normal periods · there's Deluxe Pool View, Deluxe Pool Access (step straight down to the pool), Deluxe Triple, the Kids Suite with a bunk-bed kids' room and two bathrooms, and suite-class rooms for couples or larger families · prices rise in high season, so compare several platforms before booking

faq.q: Who does X10 Khaolak Resort suit best?
faq.a: It's a great fit for families travelling with kids, with 5 pools, slides, kids' pools, a kids club, and a bunk-bed Kids Suite · at the same time it suits couples who want a beachfront resort on an attainable budget, thanks to the separate adults-only beachfront pool that gives a quiet space · if you're after a small, quiet resort focused on maximum privacy, The Sarojin or Casa de la Flora may suit you better

faq.q: What pools and activities does X10 Khaolak Resort have?
faq.a: It has 5 pools across both wings, including 2 kids' pools with slides and a splash zone, and the pool closest to the beach reserved for adults only (under-16s not allowed) · there's a swim-up pool bar, a beach bar, The Sun Spa, a fitness and aerobics room, a kids club, pool and ping-pong tables, and non-motorized water activities

faq.q: What's the food like at X10 Khaolak Resort?
faq.a: The main restaurant is Seaside Seafood Kitchen, an open terrace on the beach serving seafood and Thai food that many reviews praise as tasty and made with care · breakfast is a varied buffet with both Asian and Western options · some voices say the dinner is a buffet at certain times with options that may feel repetitive for guests on a long stay · it's worth heading out to try places around Bang Niang or Nang Thong now and then

faq.q: How far ahead should you book, and is cancellation possible?
faq.a: In high season (November–April) you should book at least 1 month ahead, especially if you want a Pool Access or Kids Suite room · every platform usually has a Free Cancellation option — pick that first if your plans aren't firm yet, then compare Agoda / Booking / Trip.com prices before confirming
